questions.question: Why is an HTTP success rate insufficient as the primary GenAI health signal?
options: A request can succeed technically while its answer, cost, latency, safety, or user outcome is unacceptable.
HTTP responses never include status codes for model requests.
Every successful request has exactly the same token cost.
Infrastructure metrics already contain the full prompt and response.
questions.explanation: Transport success covers only one layer; production health also depends on execution behavior and user-visible outcomes.

questions.question: What is the core invariant of a production GenAI deployment?
options: Every request and release must remain bounded, observable, attributable to a version, and reversible to a known-good path
Every request must use the newest model available
Infrastructure uptime is sufficient evidence of answer quality
Autoscaling should eliminate all admission limits
questions.explanation: A production deployment needs control over serving demand and release risk. Version identity, explicit budgets, production evidence, and a tested fallback make failures containable.

questions.question: Which statement is the core security invariant for a tool-using agent?
options: A model proposal has no authority until external policy authorizes a scoped action.
A confident model may grant itself temporary permissions.
Valid JSON arguments prove that a tool call is safe.
A safe final answer makes intermediate tool calls irrelevant.
questions.explanation: The model may propose actions, but authenticated identity, authorization, intent, limits, approval, and execution policy must be enforced outside it.

questions.question: What is the core invariant of an operational AI governance system?
options: Every material decision connects a system version and risk to an owner, evidence, control, decision, and follow-up action.
Every AI system uses the same control checklist.
A legal policy page exists before launch.
The model provider owns every downstream application risk.
questions.explanation: Traceable accountability lets a reviewer reconstruct what was assessed, who decided, which conditions applied, and what happened next.
